iterations.explanation: Five orthogonal dimensions: consistency/replication (state semantics), maintenance placement (load tradeoffs), storage substrate (object persistence), constraint framing (dominant bottlenecks), and pets-vs-cattle operations (management philosophy).

clusters.name: Consistency and Replication Model Choice
clusters.description: Distinguishes architectures by how repository state updates propagate across replicas (strong vs consensus-style replication) rather than how objects are stored or maintained.

relations.rationale: Strong/consensus replication choices typically shape where maintenance work can be centralized (e.g., primary/leader) versus distributed.

values.label: Strongly consistent replica visibility
values.description: Repository hosting replication must provide strong consistency, avoiding eventual consistency for clients’ update visibility.

values.label: Consensus-replicated repository hosting
values.description: Replica set uses consensus replication so real repositories behave as replicated state across nodes.

clusters.name: Replica Maintenance and Compaction Placement
clusters.description: Distinguishes designs by who performs expensive upkeep (e.g., compaction) and resulting load trade-offs between primary and replicas.

relations.rationale: Maintenance placement and consistency/replication mechanisms co-occur in designs targeting correctness at scale.

values.label: Primary-only compaction
values.description: Run compaction only on the primary, reducing replica CPU while increasing bandwidth usage on replicas to receive effects.

clusters.name: Underlying Storage Substrate Strategy
clusters.description: Distinguishes architectures by what lower-level storage substrate holds Git objects (filesystem distribution, distributed key-value store, or redesigned hosting layers).

relations.rationale: Choosing a storage substrate like a distributed KV store can constrain feasible correctness/replication models compared to designing hosting layers.

values.label: Replace filesystem distribution with Spokes
values.description: Move from filesystem-based distribution experiments to a dedicated repository hosting system (Spokes) for real replicated repos.

values.label: Distributed key-value store for objects rejected
values.description: Explicitly rejected idea of storing Git objects for hosting scaling in a distributed key-value store.

values.label: Distributed filesystem under Git rejected
values.description: Explicitly rejects using a distributed filesystem as the storage substrate beneath Git, preferring different hosting-layer redesign.

clusters.name: Scaling Tradeoff Framing and Constraints
clusters.description: Distinguishes documents by the stated dominant constraints and balancing act (performance vs correctness vs operational complexity) when scaling Git hosting.

relations.rationale: Constraint framing about object distribution/access patterns drives which storage/substrate approaches are viable.

values.label: Object distribution/access-patterns limit scalability
values.description: Scaling is constrained by how Git objects must be distributed and accessed under real workloads and replica/caching effects.

values.label: Central correctness costs increase with distribution
values.description: Maintaining correctness/consistency becomes expensive when replicas and caches are introduced, requiring deliberate trade-offs.

values.label: Performance–correctness–operations balancing
values.description: Architectural decisions explicitly balance performance, correctness, and operational complexity rather than optimizing one dimension alone.

values.label: Multiple alternatives evaluated for scaling
values.description: Context emphasizes comparing alternative solutions for scaling Git hosting rather than adopting a single approach without analysis.

clusters.name: Reliability and Operations Philosophy (Pets vs Cattle)
clusters.description: Distinguishes how systems treat replicated repository nodes as operationally managed state (stateful “pets”) versus generic scalable compute (“cattle”).

relations.rationale: Treating replicas as stateful pets aligns with strong correctness/replication mechanisms requiring careful management.

values.label: Consensus replicas treated as stateful pets
values.description: Design treats consensus-replicated repository hosting as “pets”: stateful, carefully managed, not generic auto-scalable cattle.

iterations.explanation: Updated the consistency axis to include WAL-derived truth derivation and relaxed consensus. Expanded the substrate axis to capture S3-backed WAL storage, client-side Git virtualization, and a rejected blob+RDBMS option. Added tail-latency and replica-count/cost tradeoffs, plus an automation+coordination framing. Kept existing dimensions where still orthogonal (maintenance placement, pets-vs-cattle). No dimension count increase (stayed at 5).

values.label: Strongly consistent replica visibility

values.label: Relaxed replica consensus for scalability

clusters.name: Underlying Storage Substrate Strategy

values.label: Distributed object-store for hosting scaling experiments

values.label: S3-backed write-ahead logs for repository state

values.label: Rejected blob-storage plus relational-database alternative

values.label: Client-side Git virtualization as effective storage/substrate shift
values.description: Shifts repository state access burden to clients via virtualization/caching (e.g., GVFS/Scalar) rather than server replication storage.

saturation_history.rationale:
All relevant open codes are already covered by existing taxonomy dimensions:
- Alternative evaluation context (“Multiple architectural alternatives evaluated…”) is covered by Dimension 4 (Scaling Tradeoff Framing and Constraints), which explicitly includes comparing alternatives.
- Rejected designs (“distributed filesystem under Git rejected”, “store Git objects in a distributed key-value store rejected”) and substrate redirection (“prefer redesigning consistency/replication layers over storage substrate”, “Spokes replaced filesystem-based repository distribution”) are covered by Dimension 3 (Underlying Storage Substrate Strategy), including explicit rejection/alternative substrate choices and Spokes replacing filesystem distribution.
- Scaling constrained by object distribution/access patterns and the tradeoff framing (constraints limiting scalability; centralized correctness cost with distribution; balancing performance/correctness/operations) are all covered by Dimension 4.
- Strong consistency requirement is covered by Dimension 1 (Consistency and Replication Model Choice), specifically the strong/avoid eventual visibility axis.
- Replica maintenance placement (“primary-only compaction…”) is covered by Dimension 2 (Replica Maintenance and Compaction Placement).
- Consensus replication for hosting real repositories and treating replicated repositories as first-class state are covered by Dimension 1 (Consensus-replicated repository hosting) and relate to Dimension 5 (pets vs cattle) as additional operational framing, but they are already subsumed under Dimension 1 for the core consistency/replication model.
Therefore, no open codes introduce a genuinely new architectural dimension beyond what the taxonomy already captures.

uncovered_concepts: Shift from consensus-before-operations to write-ahead logging
Derive repository truth after the fact (“deriving truth later”)
Consistency achieved via WAL ordering rather than synchronous agreement
Three-phase write design to manage tail-at-scale write latency
Replace Spokes consensus replication with S3-backed write-ahead logs
Use S3 write-ahead logging as the consistency driver for repository state
saturation_history.rationale:
Most codes are covered by existing dimensions:
- “Rejected blob storage + relational DB alternative” is covered by the existing storage-substrate rejection (3.4).
- “Client-side Git virtualization (GVFS/Scalar) … reduce server burden” / “Avoids increasing server replication/consistency … as primary scaling strategy” are covered by Client-side virtualization (3.5) and by the scaling constraint framing (4.8).
- Spokes consensus replication and the replica management framing for correctness/cost are covered by Consistency/Replication model choice (1.2, 1.4) plus Replica-count/cost tradeoff (4.6).
- “Safe minimum replica count requirement” is also covered by 4.6.
- “Distributed-object-store replication experiment … intermediate step” is covered by 3.2.
- “AI-driven automation … client/server coordination emphasis” is covered by 4.7.

However, several WAL/Continuity/Origin-specific codes are not fully absorbed:
- The taxonomy has a value for “WAL-driven eventual truth derivation” (1.3) and for “S3-backed write-ahead logs …” (3.3), but the minibatch contains multiple closely related, finer-grained WAL design intents (e.g., shifting from consensus-before-operations to deriving truth later; consistency via WAL ordering; replacing Spokes consensus replication with S3 WAL as the driver). None of the existing values/dimensions explicitly capture these as the central architectural axis beyond the coarse labels.
- The “three-phase write design to manage tail-at-scale write latency” is not covered: the closest existing element is the tail-latency tradeoff driver (4.5), but there is no value encoding the specific three-phase write pipeline structure as an axis/variant.

Therefore, with the conservative saturation rule, the taxonomy is not yet saturated against the full set of open codes.
